title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows, optimize cache and dependency hygiene
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: CI runtime and flakiness on the monorepo have crept up as we added more packages and test targets. This PR refactors the CI workflows to separate concerns (lint, test, release) so each pipeline is easier to reason about, can be scheduled independently, and benefits from more targeted caching. It also performs dependency hygiene for dev tooling (upgrade actions and linters), fixes cache key collisions, and removes deprecated workflow steps. Key changes: 1) Split .github/workflows into lint.yml, test.yml, and release.yml with a shared common workflow template for setup/caching. 2) Improve caching semantics: cache per-package-lock hash + node-version + job-type to reduce stale cache hits; added fallback warm-up runs. 3) Upgrade GitHub Actions and Node tool versions used by CI (actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4, node 20) and bump several devDeps (eslint, typescript, jest) to latest minor patches to address security/hygiene alerts. 4) Release automation: move publish step into release.yml, add explicit permission scoping and a manual approval gate for production releases. 5) Reduce test matrix footprint by grouping integration tests into a smaller matrix and adding a quick smoke job for PRs. Checklist: - [x] Split workflows + common template - [x] Implement improved cache keys and verify cache hit stats - [x] Bump actions and devDeps with changelog review - [x] Run full CI across main and release branches - [x] Add branch protection note for new release gate Testing and rollout: ran workflows on feature branch and a production dry-run; addressed a cache collision that caused intermittent install failures. No runtime code changes. Release notes: CI and tooling refactor; developer UX improvements for PR feedback loops.
